Information Note to the Press (Press Release No.   143 / 2026) 
TELECOM REGULATORY AUTHORITY OF INDIA 
www.trai.gov.in 
New Delhi, 30 Oct 2026 
For Immediate Release 
 
TRAI Assesses Mobile Network Quality  Across Lakjung, Tsati, Yurtung, Kushok Bakula Rimpochee 
Airport, Leh Palace, Sankar Gompa, Leh, Choglamsar and Spituk  etc. under Leh (Ladakh) and nearby 
areas. 
The Telecom Regulatory  Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive 
Test (IDT) conducted across Leh and nearby areas route under J&K LSA, during the month of Aug 2026, 
for information of general telecom consumers.  The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real 
time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers  
(TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters 
like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload 
(UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their 
services. 
2. These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs 
across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc.  In this type of drive 
testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards  from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 
5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analy zed in 
real-time using advanced Software Systems. 
3. TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 62.6 Km, Hotspot 
locations - 07, Walk Test - 1.1 Km, Inter Operator Calling at 01 location and on Highway drive - 396.3 Km 
during 17th Aug 2026 to 21st Aug 2026 in J&K LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision 
of the  TRAI Regional Office Delhi.  The observations presented  in drive test  reports represent the 
performance of the TSPs on the area / route under test on the day / time of conducting the drive test.  
4. Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating 
City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots, Walk test & Highways drive as per the legends shown on 
the map: -

5. Key Parameters Assessed 
a) Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the  
minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G). 
b) Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, 
Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS). 
c) Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instances occurred during the calls. 
d) Data Services: Download / Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate. 
6. The overall mobile network performance in Leh, Nubra Valley and Pangong areas route for the 
key parameters has been summarized below: - 
a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in 
auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal 
strength out of the total samples collected, was 583/9318 for Airtel, 966/8977 for BSNL & 
770/8371 for RJIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-
I. 
 
b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto -selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the 
number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/83 for 
Airtel, 5/77 for BSNL & 1/76 for RJIL.  Details of the dropped call locations have been 
provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as 
the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, 
were 2/75 for Airtel, 2/75 for BSNL & 1/72 for RJIL. Details of the call silence instance 
locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
d) Data Download and Upload Throughput: 
i) Data Download performance (Overall):  Average download speed was observed as 1 21.65 
Mbps for Airtel (5G), 8.00 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 267.13 Mbps for RJIL (5G).  Detail of 
Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
 
ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 22.13 Mbps for 
Airtel (5G), 4.87 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 21.20 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Details of Upload 
throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-I. 
 
Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of 
Annexure-I. 
7. The overall mobile network performance on Leh to Nubra Valley h i g h wa y route for the key 
parameters has been summarized below: - 
a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in 
auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal 
strength out of the total samples collected, was 4040/11146 for Airtel, 3361/11313 for BSNL 
& 3530/9209 for RJIL.  Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of 
Annexure-II. 
 
b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto -selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the 
number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 12/108 for 
Airtel, 13/95 for BSNL & 4/85 for RJIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been 
provided in the map of Annexure-II. 
c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as 
the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, 
were 14/91 for Airtel, 6/71 for BSNL & 16/78 for RJIL. Details of the call silence instance 
locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

d) Data Download and Upload Throughput: 
i) Data Download performance (Overall):  Average download speed was observed as 109.57 
Mbps for Airtel (5G), 16.39 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 122.16 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Detail of 
Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-II. 
 
ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.21 Mbps for 
Airtel (5G), 7.81 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 12.02 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Details of Upload 
throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-II. 
 
Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of 
Annexure-II. 
8. The overall mobile network performance o n  Nubra Valley to Pangong highway route  for the 
key parameters has been summarized below: - 
a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in 
auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal 
strength out of the total samples collected, was 4950/12272 for Airtel, 3203/12041 for BSNL 
& 5105/9930 for RJIL.  Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of 
Annexure-III. 
 
b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto -selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the 
number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 11/67 for 
Airtel, 17/64 for BSNL & 16/60 for RJIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been 
provided in the map of Annexure-III. 
c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as 
the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, 
were 18/66 for Airtel, 16/59 for BSNL & 24/52 for RJIL. Details of the call silence instance 
locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-III. 
d) Data Download and Upload Throughput: 
i) Data Download performance (Overall):  Average download speed was observed as 80.59 
Mbps for Airtel (5G), 8.86 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 44.48 Mbps for RJIL (5G).  Detail of 
Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-III. 
 
ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.69 Mbps for 
Airtel (5G), 3.51 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 3.94 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Details of Upload 
throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-III. 
 
Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of 
Annexure-III. 
9. The overall mobile network performance o n  Sakti to Sangam highway for the key parameters 
has been summarized below: - 
a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in 
auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal 
strength out of the total samples collected, was  800/6295 for Airtel, 2140/6252 for BSNL &  
893/5597 for RJIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-
IV. 
 
b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto -selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the 
number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 1/32 for 
Airtel, 5/27 for BSNL & 2 /30 for RJIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been 
provided in the map of Annexure-IV. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
10. 
Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 2/31 for Airtel, 15/26 for BSNL & 5/30 for RJIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV. 
Data Download and Upload Throughput: Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 96.97 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 6.00 Mbps for BSNL (4G), and 203.25 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Detail of 
Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-IV. 
ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 14.67 Mbps for 
Airtel (5G), 4.14 Mbps for BSNL (4G) & 18.84 Mbps for RJIL (5G). Details of Upload 
throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-IV. 
Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of 
Annexure-IV. 
Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as below: -
a) City - The areas covered in the city drive are Lakjung, Tsati, Yurtung, Kushok Bakula 
Rimpochee Airport, Leh Palace, Sankar Gompa, Leh, Choglamsar and Spituk etc. under Leh 
and nearby areas. 
b) Highway - The area covered in the highway route are Leh to Nubra Valley via Power House, 
View Point Khadungla road, South Pullu, Shiv Shankar Temple, North Pullu, Khardung 
Viewpoint, Khalsar and Diskit etc., Nubra Valley to Pangong via Tsati, Agham, Sakti, Zingral, 
Tsoltak, Tangtse, Muglib, Spangmik and Pangong beach etc. & Sakti to Sangam via Chemrey, 
Karu, Thiksey, Shey, Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport, Indus Viewpoint and Sangam Point 
Leh Ladakh etc. 
c) Hotspot - The hotspot locations, capturing stationary user experience are Army Hospital 
Hundar, Artisan Bazaar, EJM College, Gurudwara Sri Pathar Sahib, Leh Airport, Leh Market 
& SNM Hospital. 
d) Walk Test - The walk test conducted on 17h Aug 2026, covered Leh Market capturing mobile 
network behaviors in crowded pedestrian environments. 
14. The findings of this IDT report have been shared with respective TSPs for taking further necessary 
action at their end. Detailed reports of IDT are made available on the TRAI website at www.trai.gov.in. For any clarification or additional infornation, an email can be sent to adv.ca@trai.gov. in or Regional Office of TRAI at Delhi RO can be contacted on Telephone No. +91-11-20907772.
